fixes.explanation: Right, baker. He asks if His hand is too short and if He lacks the strength to deliver, and then He answers with a show of power. "Behold, My rebuke dries up the sea; I turn the rivers into a desert…" Nothing in these verses says His strength has run out.
That's right, baker. The LORD says, "I clothe the heavens in black and make sackcloth their covering." The sea is dry, the rivers are desert, and now the sky is dressed in black. He just keeps going.

That's the one, baker. The speaker says, "He awakens Me morning by morning; He awakens My ear to listen as a disciple." Morning after morning, the ear gets woken up to listen. You know how people hit the snooze button about every round? Nobody's proud of that.
The verse says the opposite, friend. "The One who vindicates Me is near." Near, not far off. Right after that, the speaker asks, "Who will dare to contend with Me?"
A field is a solid guess, friend. But not here. The verse says, "…they will all wear out like a garment; the moths will devour them." The word is garment.

Right, baker. The verse says, "Let him trust in the name of the LORD; let him lean on his God." The person in the dark with no light is told to trust and to lean. Those are the two things the verse says.

That's what the verse says, baker. "You will lie down in a place of torment." This one is heavy. It's spoken to those who kindle a fire and array themselves with firebrands, and who are told to walk in the light of their fire.

Rest would be a nice thing to hear, friend, but that's not what the verse says. The words are, "You will lie down in a place of torment." It's a heavy verse. It speaks to those who kindle fires and are told to walk in the light of their fire.

I understand why it might sound that way, since these people kindle fires and array themselves with firebrands. But the verse says, "You will lie down in a place of torment." That's the word from His hand. It's a heavy verse.
